also: take good care of your health!

evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: valētūdinem tuam velim cūrēs dīligentissimē
Traupman 63: Cūrā dīligenter valētūdinem tuam!, take good care of your health!
terms.comment: On its own it can mean either; bona valētūdō is good health, adversa, mala, īnfirma valētūdō ill health (Traupman 64). How someone is goes with the verb: valeō, I’m well; valētūdinem cūrāre, to look after one’s health.

terms.gloss: be well, be in good health
evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō
terms.comment: The verb Latin prefers: ut valēs?, how are you?; cūrā ut valeās, look after yourself.

evidence: Plaut. Merc. 678–679: salūtem et sānitātem nostrae familiae
terms.comment: Soundness of body; in Cicero also soundness of mind.

evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.1.108: praecipuē sānus, nisi cum pītuīta molesta est
terms.comment: Food that is good for you is salūbris (see healthy).

evidence: Cato Agr. 141.3: bonam salūtem valētūdinemque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Wider than valētūdō: wellbeing and safety; also the greeting of a letter (salūtem dīcere).

evidence: Traupman 64: salvus et validus, hale and hearty
terms.comment: Strong and well: the opposite is imbēcillus or īnfirmus.

phrases.latin: sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō. valētūdinem tuam velim cūrēs dīligentissimē
phrases.english: if you are well, good; I am well. Please look after your health with the greatest care

phrases.latin: valētūdō sustentātur nōtitiā suī corporis et observātiōne, quae rēs aut prōdesse soleant aut obesse
phrases.english: health is kept up by knowing one’s own body and noticing what usually does it good or harm

phrases.latin: ipse melior fīō, prīmum valētūdine, quam intermissīs exercitātiōnibus āmīseram
phrases.english: I am getting better myself: first in health, which I had lost by giving up my exercise

phrases.latin: nōn est vīvere, sed valēre vīta est
phrases.english: life is not just being alive, but being well
